rows.text: Toxicity has two mechanisms and five names. **Mechanism one — soft-metal sulphur binding:** As(III), Hg²⁺, Pb²⁺ and Cd²⁺ all latch onto the –SH groups of enzymes (arsenicosis from >10 ppb groundwater; **Minamata disease** from methylmercury that bioaccumulates in fish and destroys the CNS).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - WHO arsenic limit in drinking water: 10 ppb (0.01 mg/L) - As(III) + enzyme –SH groups → blocked enzymes - Chelation antidotes: EDTA (Pb); BAL/dimercaprol (As, Hg); penicillamine (Cu); desferrioxamine (Fe)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: metal toxicity, toxicity due to iron, arsenic, mercury (within Bio-inorganic Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Lead inhibits the enzymes of haem synthesis and damages the nervous system of children, while methylmercury attacks the central nervous system and bioaccumulates in fish."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Minamata, 1956*** — a factory's mercury effluent became methylmercury in the bay's bacteria, concentrated through the fish chain, and struck the fishing town's nervous system: bioaccumulation made a trace pollutant into a mass poisoning.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — When the Metal Is the Poison The same d-block chemistry that makes Fe, Cu and Zn essential makes Pb, Hg, Cd and As dangerous: they bind sulphur and other biological ligands where they do not belong, or imitate essential ions and hijack their machinery. The syllabus names five toxic metals — **Fe (in excess), As, Hg, Pb, Cd** — each with a classic disease story and a chemistry explanation.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Iron — essential metal, toxic in excess - **Overdose** (especially iron tonic tablets in children) causes gastrointestinal corrosion, liver damage and death; free Fe²⁺ catalyses formation of damaging radicals (Fenton chemistry) and overwhelms transport proteins.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Disease map: Fe-haemochromatosis, As-arsenicosis (10 ppb), Hg-Minamata (CNS), Pb-anaemia+IQ (mimics Ca), Cd-itai-itai (kidney, mimics Zn). Antidotes: EDTA-Pb, BAL-As/Hg, penicillamine-Cu, desferrioxamine-Fe.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Write the harmful effects of lead and mercury on human health.** — **Lead:** Pb²⁺ enters the body through lead-painted dust, contaminated water and pipes, battery recycling and (formerly) leaded petrol.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Why is arsenic-contaminated groundwater dangerous, and what disease does chronic exposure cause?** — Arsenic in groundwater occurs mainly as **arsenite, As(III)**, a soft Lewis acid that binds the **–SH (thiol) groups of enzymes** and blocks them, besides disrupting energy metabolism.…

rows.text: For lead and mercury, give the route (paint/petrol vs fish/vapour), the target (blood/children vs CNS) and one named effect each — three pairs of facts, one mark each.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Two poisoning strategies: soft metals (Hg, Pb, Cd, As(III)) bind the soft sulphur of cysteine and disable enzymes wholesale, while mimicry (Pb2+ as Ca2+, Cd2+ as Zn2+) lets them sneak into the wrong seats — and chelation therapy wins by out-gripping both.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Iron excess: overdose (children's tonics) -> gut corrosion, liver damage; chronic overload = haemochromatosis (liver/pancreas/heart); chelator desferrioxamine. Arsenic: As(III) binds -SH groups of enzymes; arsenicosis = skin lesions + cancer + neuropathy; groundwater hazard, WHO limit 10 ppb (Nepal Terai affected).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The WHO limit for arsenic in drinking water is 10 ppb (0.01 mg/L); tube-well groundwater above this limit affects millions across the Gangetic plain including Nepal's Terai.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Name the disease caused by cadmium poisoning and explain why cadmium is toxic.** — Chronic cadmium poisoning causes **itai-itai disease** ("ouch-ouch", Japan) — severe kidney damage together with painful **bone decalcification** and fractures.…

Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Haemochromatosis** | Chronic iron-overload disease | iron deposits in liver/pancreas | | **Arsenicosis** | Chronic arsenic poisoning via water/food | skin lesions, cancer | | **Minamata disease** | Methylmercury poisoning from contaminated fish | Japan, 1950s | | **Itai-itai disease** |…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why soft metals attack sulphur - Hg²⁺, Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺ and As(III) are **soft/borderline Lewis acids** with high affinity for the **soft –SH sulphur** of cysteine residues. Binding an enzyme's essential cysteine disables it.…  ·  ## 5. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: What is chelation therapy and why must the antidote ligand bind the metal more strongly than the enzyme does?  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Mercury's danger is the organic form and vapour, not liquid contact:** liquid metallic mercury swallowed in small amount passes through the gut largely unabsorbed; the vapour and methylmercury are the killers.  ·  **Iron toxicity is about dose, not identity:** iron is essential; its toxicity (overdose, haemochromatosis) is the dose rule of row 91 seen from the other side.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Minamata = mercury, itai-itai = cadmium:** the two Japanese disease names are the most-swapped pair in the exam — mercury ate the nerves, cadmium ate the kidneys and bones.  ·  ## 7.
